::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
**I am on the job market** for postdoctoral and research scientist positions starting in 2027.
If my work fits your group, please [get in touch](mailto:polejua@email.sc.edu).
:::

I am a Ph.D. candidate in Biostatistics at the Arnold School of Public Health, University of
South Carolina, advised by Dr. Alexander McLain. I expect to graduate in May 2027. I live in
the Dallas–Fort Worth area of Texas.

My work is in **functional data analysis** and **scalable Bayesian methods**. Wearable devices
record activity minute by minute, for days or weeks, so each person gives a curve instead of a
single number. I develop and apply methods that use the whole curve, and I write them as
software that other people can use.

## What I work on

::: {.card-row}
::: {.item}
#### Variational Bayes for high-dimensional regression
Fast Bayesian variable selection with spike-and-slab priors that keeps the uncertainty
honest. R package `spexvb` on CRAN.
:::
::: {.item}
#### Scalar-on-function regression
Bayesian regression where the predictor is a curve, for example 24-hour activity from a
wrist accelerometer.
:::
::: {.item}
#### Wearable and accelerometer data
Clustering 24-hour activity patterns, processing raw accelerometer data with GGIR, and
measuring the bias of non-wear imputation.
:::
:::

## Where I am going

I want to see statistical methods used in the world, not only published. My goal is to work
with functional data from wearable devices, developing methods and applying my own methods and
those of others, so that practitioners can use them. That can happen in academia or in a
company that builds wearable devices. More in [my own words](story.qmd).
